title: Selective DREADD-based Chemogenetic Inhibition of GABAergic Neurons in Rats
author: Cicciarelli, Concina, et al.

steps.title: House and acclimate rats
steps.instruction: House healthy male Sprague‑Dawley rats (age 65–70 days; weight 240–350 g) in plastic cages (2–3 rats per cage) with food and water ad libitum, under a 12 h light/dark cycle (lights on at 07:00 a.m.) at a constant temperature of 22 ± 1 °C. Begin this preparation months before the experiment.

steps.title: Prepare viral stocks
steps.instruction: Use the trans‑synaptic Cre virus AAV1‑hSyn‑Cre (titer 2 × 10^13 GC/mL) and the Cre‑dependent inhibitory DREADD virus AAV1‑hDlx‑DIO‑KORD‑mCyRFP (titer 4 × 10^12 GC/mL). Aliquot each viral preparation into sterile Eppendorf tubes and store at –80 °C until the day of injection. This preparation should be done at least one week before the experiment.

steps.title: Sterilize instruments and set up stereotaxic infusion
steps.instruction: Sterilize all surgical instruments and work surfaces with 70 % ethanol. Assemble the stereotaxic apparatus. Thaw the viral aliquots on ice. Load a 10 µL Hamilton syringe fitted with a 28‑gauge needle onto an infusion pump. Set the infusion rate to between 0.1 and 0.3 µL/min. Perform these actions 1 hour before surgery.

steps.title: Prepare fixation and immunostaining solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the following reagents at the indicated final concentrations: Paraformaldehyde 4 %; PBS; 0,12 M sucrose 30 %; anti‑RFP 1:500; anti‑GAD65/67 1:1000; Cy3 anti‑guinea‑pig 1:1000; Alexa Fluor 488 anti‑rabbit 1:1000; DAPI 1:1000.

steps.title: Acquire BLA confocal images
steps.instruction: Using a Zeiss Airyscan confocal microscope, capture images of the basolateral amygdala (BLA) at anterior‑posterior coordinates 2.4 mm to 3.5 mm from bregma. Employ three lasers (405 nm, 488 nm, 568 nm) matched to the emission peaks of DAPI (nuclear stain), Alexa Fluor 488, and mCyRFP, respectively. Acquire image stacks with a 40× objective, 15 sections spaced 1.5 µm apart. Timing for this step is variable.

steps.title: Process images and quantify cell populations
steps.instruction: Analyze the acquired images with ImageJ software. Count KORD‑expressing cells (mCyRFP) and GAD65/67‑expressing cells (Alexa 488). Normalize each cell count to the total number of DAPI‑positive cells.

steps.title: Conduct statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Perform statistical analysis using SPSS Statistics 22 (IBM) and generate graphs. Estimate required sample size with G*Power based on effect‑size calculations. Test for normality with the Kolmogorov‑Smirnov test. For normally distributed data, compare two groups using two‑tailed unpaired Student’s t‑tests. Consider results significant when p < 0.05 (∗p < 0.05, ∗∗p < 0.01, ∗∗∗p < 0.001, ∗∗∗∗p < 0.0001). Present data as mean ± SEM.

description: Chemogenetic technique allows researchers to manipulate excitable cells by controlling their activity. Along with optogenetic, this technique has been extremely valuable to dissect and comprehend neuronal circuits’ architecture, activity and regulation.2,3,4,5,6,7 The strength of these methods lies in the flexibility of the viral vectors which allow a plethora of manipulation strategies. Among them, recombinant adeno associated viral vectors (rAAVs) are widely used in neuroscience because their tropism, transduction, and gene expression system can be easily modified.8 Several viral serotypes exhibit both anterograde and retrograde transduction capabilities, enabling the study of neuronal circuits among distant structures.8 An important advantage of rAAVs is the possibility to control gene expression through Cre-lox genetic switches, such as double-floxed inverted open-reading frame (DIO), or FLip-EXcision (FLEx) approaches.8 Combinatorial dual AAV vector techniques have been extensively used to decipher and manipulate neural circuits in the brain, and are based on two vectors, one expressing Cre recombinase and the other one expressing Cre-dependent transgene.9,10,11 The possibility to use also neuronal subtype-specific promoters allow researchers to study circuits in a very detailed way.10,12 This protocol describes how to identify and manipulate the anatomical and functional relationship between two selected brain structures, with a particular focus on the connections between a starter neural site and specific target neuronal cell types involved in defined behavioral or physiological functions. Specifically, this protocol focuses on the ability of hippocampal projecting neurons to regulate GABAergic neurons in the basolateral amygdala in rats during segregation of remote fear memories. These brain sites are selected as their well-defined role in the encoding of fear memories, together with other brain regions such as the sensory cortices.13,14,15,16
